asil_justification.open_item: If commissioning were ever to be brought inside a defined operational situation - a workshop scenario with occupants, for instance - the reason above would no longer hold and the requirement would need an ASIL allocation. This field does not claim that case has been analysed.
asil_justification.reason: This requirement is classified 'safety', which is the reason the marking is recorded explicitly rather than left implicit. It constrains the commissioning and service mode: no high-voltage contactor is commanded closed without an explicit commissioning command, and an unconnected sensor input is diagnosed rather than read as a cell at a limit. The failure mode it guards against is an energisation on unconnected or untrusted input, which occurs during production and service rather than as a runtime hazard of a defined operational situation.
asil_justification.scope_of_this_classification: This field records why safety_allocation.asil is not_applicable on this requirement. It is a statement about this record's own allocation bookkeeping inside a fictional reference project. It is not a determination about the real foxBMS 2 product and not a claim that the commissioning mode has been shown to be safe.
what_this_does_not_assert: It does not assert conformity with ISO 26262, and it is not a certification, a type approval, or evidence of one. Nothing in this field was audited to produce it.

It does not assert human approval. human_approval_status on this record is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false, and no functional-safety expert has confirmed any of it.
It does not establish that any ASIL was correctly assigned to any safety requirement in this corpus. It explains only why this requirement is not itself an ASIL-allocated item.
It does not assert tool qualification. No tool used anywhere in this corpus has been qualified for a safety purpose.
It does not assert an ASPICE capability level for anything.
asil_justification.why_not_an_asil_allocation: An ASIL in ISO 26262 is assigned to a safety requirement derived from a hazardous event identified for a defined operational situation. Commissioning and service are not such an operational situation: they are activities outside the defined runtime operation, and a failure there is a production escape rather than a hazardous event. The schema's enumerated value not_applicable is used for that case. Note that this reason depends on the assumption that commissioning is genuinely outside the runtime operational situations defined by the project's HARA; the corpus records that assumption as FB2-ASM-011.

record_verbatim.rationale: The system-level requirement behind the commissioning mode, and the one that carries the service-class stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000005 into the item's architecture. Its second half is deliberately a cybersecurity requirement appearing at system level: the framing and authorisation of the service link is a property of the integrated item's interfaces, not of one module, and the security requirement FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 constrains the same link from the other direction. Both halves exist because the failure they guard against is the one a production or service error produces, and no safety requirement in this corpus covers it.

revision_history.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

record_verbatim.statement: While the item is in its commissioning mode, no high-voltage contactor shall be commanded closed unless an explicit commissioning command is present, and an open-circuit or unconnected sensor input shall be diagnosed as such and shall not be interpreted as a cell at a limit; on leaving commissioning, the item shall return to a state in which no contactor actuation is possible without a current-flow request. Bytes received on a service link shall be acted upon only inside a validated, authenticated frame.
